record.original_question: Among all argumentation frameworks with n arguments and k attacks, let sigma(n,k) be the average number of stable extensions. Determine a sufficiently precise or closed-form expression for sigma(n,k), including the middle range of k where the average number of stable extensions first decreases, then increases, and then decreases again.

evidence.quote: What is the average number of extensions for an AF possessing n arguments and k attacks?
The main open problem of this section is a sufficiently precise specification of the function σ(n, k).
Open Problem 5 What is σ(n, k)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An argumentation framework is a finite directed graph $F=(A,R)$, where $A$ is a set of $n$ arguments (vertices) and $R\subseteq A\times A$ is a set of $k$ attacks (directed edges, including possible self-loops). A subset $S\subseteq A$ is called a stable extension of $F$ if:
(i) $S$ is conflict-free, i.e., there are no $a,b\in S$ with $(a,b)\in R$; and
(ii) $S$ attacks every argument outside it, i.e., for every $a\in A\setminus S$ there exists $b\in S$ with $(b,a)\in R$.

Let $\mathcal{F}(n,k)$ denote the set of all argumentation frameworks on a fixed labeled vertex set of size $n$ having exactly $k$ attacks, and for $F\in\mathcal{F}(n,k)$ let $\operatorname{st}(F)$ denote the number of stable extensions of $F$. Define
$$\sigma(n,k)\;=\;\frac{1}{|\mathcal{F}(n,k)|}\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(n,k)}\operatorname{st}(F).$$

Determine a sufficiently precise (ideally closed-form) expression for $\sigma(n,k)$ as a function of $n$ and $k$. In particular, give an analytic description of the behavior of $\sigma(n,\cdot)$ throughout the full range $0\le k\le n^{2}$, including the middle range of $k$ where empirically $\sigma(n,k)$ first decreases, then increases, and then decreases again.
artifact.status_search_result: A precise closed-form for σ(n,k) is not known. Existing work (e.g., the TAFA-13 study "On the Maximal and Average Numbers of Stable Extensions") provides a tight upper bound on the maximal number of stable extensions and empirical observations of a universal distribution shape (decrease–increase–decrease) as k varies, but does not give an analytic formula for σ(n,k); the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the Maximal and Average Numbers of Stable Extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical and empirical study of the maximal and average numbers of stable extensions; tight upper bound on the maximal number; empirical universal pattern of distribution as a function of attacks.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (empirical) results and a maximal bound are available; no closed-form for the average σ(n,k) is provided.

status_evidence.title: On the Maximal and Average Numbers of Stable Extensions (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximal and average numbers of stable extensions in abstract argumentation frameworks.
status_evidence.claim: Closest follow-up work to the open problem; addresses bounds and empirical estimation rather than an exact formula.
